title: bug: daemon HTTP /health checks no Host header, so a DNS-rebinding browser page can read the daemon's pid and project path
description: Found by worker-fe18a9a9 on CQ-RF05 (task-b439d7fb), whose decision record docs/design/protected-profile-threat-model.md places browser pages inside the threat model. Problem class: a loopback HTTP endpoint answers any Host. packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:669 serves GET /health with pid, projectPath, version and stats, and never checks req.headers.host. The WebSocket Origin rule (task-801272c4) does not cover plain HTTP. Fix direction: answer /health only for a loopback-literal or localhost Host (plus the bind address), else 403; add vitest coverage. This row sits beside the HIGH row task-724e31fa (epic-be924fb8), and the governor may move it there. Keep the row's text at problem-class level, because .moe/tasks is pushed.
definitionOfDone: GET /health with a Host other than a loopback literal, localhost or the daemon's own bind address (with or without the port) gets 403 and no body fields; the existing clients (daemon CLI probe, launchers, IDE plugins) still pass.
vitest covers the allowed and refused Host values, including an absent Host.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md or docs/ARCHITECTURE.md notes the Host rule.

implementationPlan.description:
Create packages/moe-daemon/src/server/healthHost.ts: one pure export, with no I/O and no daemon-state imports.

`export function isAllowedHealthHost(host: string | undefined, localAddress: string | undefined): boolean`

1. host undefined → true. A browser always sends Host; a request without one cannot come from a page.
2. host must match one bracketed IPv6 literal, or one token with no whitespace and none of ':/?#@[]', optionally followed by ':' and 1-5 digits whose value is 1-65535. Anything else → false.
   - The port is never compared with the daemon's port, so port forwarding keeps working.
3. Lowercase the name. A plain name equal to 'localhost' → true. Any other plain name that is not a dotted-quad IPv4 (net.isIPv4) → false. That covers every DNS name, which is what a rebinding page needs.
4. An IPv4 literal in 127.0.0.0/8 → true. A bracketed IPv6 literal (net.isIPv6 of the inner text) whose canonical form is '::1' → true. Canonicalize IPv6 with `new URL('http://[' + inner + ']').hostname`; if that throws (zone ids and the like) → false.
5. Otherwise the literal must equal the canonical localAddress → true. Before comparing:
   - strip a '::ffff:' prefix in front of a dotted IPv4;
   - canonicalize IPv6 the same way.
   This is the daemon's own bind address as the connection actually arrived on it: the WSL gateway (the Windows vEthernet adapter), an explicit --host address, or the interface a wildcard bind answered on. No interface enumeration.
6. Else → false.

error handling: the whole body is wrapped so that any throw returns false (refuse). Never log the Host value.

The header comment says:
- this is the DNS-rebinding guard for plain-HTTP GET /health;
- WebSocket upgrades are covered by the Origin rule (WebSocketServer.ts verifyClient) instead;
- 'any IP literal' was not used because the DoD refuses an IP that is not the daemon's own.

comments.content: Governor note for the planner. Several in-flight rows now depend on reading /health from outside loopback: the cross-project-attach fixes, task-86093c3e (proxy), task-90664db1 (JetBrains), task-80ed1fe8 (VS Code) and parent task-e7f4026a (wrappers), all of which read /health projectPath. In WSL agent mode, the moe-agent.sh pre-flight (`probe_daemon_health`) and the proxy reach the Windows daemon through the WSL gateway IP, e.g. `http://172.26.208.1:9876/health`, so the request's Host is an IP literal, not localhost. A DNS-rebinding defense must keep those working. Rebinding needs a hostname, so the usual rule is: accept localhost and any IP-literal Host, and refuse other names. Please cover a gateway-IP Host in the tests, and keep /health's 200/503 + projectPath contract that 86093c3e/90664db1 classify on.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Plain-HTTP GET /health answers its existing 200/503 JSON only when the request has no Host header, or its Host (port optional) is localhost, a loopback IP literal (127.0.0.0/8 or ::1), or the IP literal of the address the connection arrived on (req.socket.localAddress; an IPv4-mapped address is normalized).
- Every other Host gets 403 with Content-Type text/plain and body 'Forbidden': every DNS name, a non-loopback IP that is not the arrival address, or a malformed value.
- A page that rebinds a name to the daemon can no longer read its pid or project path.
- Loopback clients and the WSL-gateway clients keep working.
acceptanceCriteria: The real spawned daemon answers 403 'Forbidden' with no JSON to a foreign name or a foreign IP Host. It answers 200 with status, projectPath, pid, version, uptime, stats and checks to 127.0.0.1, localhost, or no Host.
probeDaemonHealth still accepts the spawned daemon, and GET /other still answers 426.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Security Notes states the Host rule.
invariants: The guard runs before any health check or stats work, and never echoes or logs the Host.
isAllowedHealthHost is pure and never throws; any parse failure refuses.
The port in Host is never compared with the daemon's port.
The 200/503 body and the 426 path are byte-identical for allowed requests.
compatibility: The proxy's daemonIdentity classifies a 403 as 'unknown' and still connects. Setting MOE_DAEMON_HOST to a DNS name now gets 403 from /health; the docs say to use an IP literal.
No MCP or WebSocket behavior changes; the Origin rule covers upgrades.
approvedScope: packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts: the import, plus the guard as the first statement of the GET /health branch.
reuse: net.isIPv4 and net.isIPv6 validate the literals, and WHATWG URL canonicalizes IPv6. No hand-written address parser.
The real-daemon rows reuse delivery/acceptance.test.ts's startDaemonChild pattern (tsx `_run`, isolated env) and the exported probeDaemonHealth.
sourceAssumptions: index.ts serves GET /health (originally at :669) with status, version, pid, uptime, projectPath, stats and checks, and answers 426 to every other plain request. task-2f2484b4 hoists that handler, shared by every listener.

Node's http server gives req.headers.host as undefined when no Host was sent (HTTP/1.0) and keeps the first of duplicate Host headers. req.socket.localAddress is the address the connection arrived on.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- The governor's 'localhost plus any IP literal' rule. Rejected for one reason: DoD 1 requires 403 for any IP that is neither loopback nor the daemon's own bind address. Comparing with req.socket.localAddress is the precise form of 'own bind address'. It keeps the governor's WSL-gateway case: in NAT mode the gateway IP is the Windows vEthernet address the connection arrives on. It needs no interface enumeration, and it works for 127.0.0.1, an explicit --host, 'wsl' and wildcard binds.
- An allowlist setting for names. Rejected: no client uses a name except localhost (YAGNI).
- Guarding every plain request. Rejected: only /health returns data; everything else is a fixed 426.
- Refusing an absent Host. Rejected: browsers always send Host, and HTTP/1.0 tools may not.
- Extracting the whole handler for in-process tests. Rejected: it rewrites the handler that task-2f2484b4 hoisted and task-2cf1c6be extended. One spawned `_run` row proves the wiring instead.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The threat-model record (docs/design/protected-profile-threat-model.md) puts browser pages in scope and files this row.
- The Origin rule (task-801272c4, WebSocketServer verifyClient) covers upgrades only.
- The proxy's daemonIdentity treats any status other than 200/503 as 'unknown' (fail-open, still connects).
- moe-agent.sh's WSL discovery tries MOE_DAEMON_HOST, then 127.0.0.1, then the gateway.
- The Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK uses localhost.
- Node keeps the first of duplicate Host headers and leaves req.headers.host undefined for HTTP/1.0 without one.
- net.isIPv4 rejects '127.1', octal, hex and decimal-integer forms.
- new URL('http://[x]').hostname canonicalizes IPv6 and throws on zone ids.
planningNotes.risks:
- index.ts is a hot file: task-2f2484b4 (WORKING), then task-2cf1c6be, then this row, serialized by dependsOn. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is also planned by CQ-RF07 (which now dependsOn this row), CQ-R13 and CQ-V12. Use the hot-file protocol.
- A NAT or port-forward setup where the client's Host IP differs from the daemon's local address (Docker -p reached by a LAN IP, a netsh portproxy) now gets 403 on /health. No such setup is documented, and localhost or 127.0.0.1 still works.
- The spawned-daemon rows are slow and platform-sensitive: bound every wait, kill the child in afterAll, never use port 9876.
- Text rule: keep everything at the problem-class level, because .moe/tasks is pushed.

New server/healthHost.ts (pure, total, 49 lines); index.ts imports it and calls it as the FIRST statement of the /health branch (+7); the 200/503 and 426 paths are unchanged; no Host is echoed or logged.

Clients: the daemon CLI probe, doctor, JetBrains DaemonIdentity, moe-agent.ps1 and the local runner send 127.0.0.1; the Docker HEALTHCHECK sends localhost; moe-agent.sh and the proxy send the host they were given (127.0.0.1 or the WSL gateway IP, which is the connection's arrival address); the proxy maps a 403 to 'unknown' and still connects.
DoD 2: table A, 44 rows: absent, localhost, 127/8, ::1, gateway IP equal to the local address (also ::ffff: dual-stack) allowed; names, foreign IPs and malformed values refused.
